title: Linear: GitHub loop triggers
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: Restraint: the UI is rebuilt at about 2.5× its size on a near-black canvas and the camera never moves; every motion is the product's own (typing, posting, scrolling), and each new line gets 1.6–2.0 s to be read before anything else moves.
instrument: Cut candidates over-count: a message appearing or the composer growing reads as a cut. The scrolls bring in new content and the title exits fade and blur, so neither fits a camera model.

byEye.zoom: one UI fragment at a time, about 2.5× native size; the composer spans ~85% of the frame width
byEye.cards: 3: 'GitHub loop triggers' 2.0 s, 'Now available' 1.4 s, the Linear logo 4.2 s (14% of the runtime); white type centred on near-black
byEye.cursor: none; typing shows by its caret
byEye.frame: full-bleed near-black canvas, no window chrome
byEye.sound: an audio track with sparse onsets (11 in 30 s); 2 of 14 cuts within 50 ms of its beat grid (chance 16%); the logo cut lands 34 ms from an onset

classify: Motion-designed changelog film with the UI rebuilt as a mock-up. Conventions: one fragment at a time at reading size, a locked frame, claim and logo cards on near-black.

diagnose.observation: The UI is rebuilt at about ×2.5 and the frame never moves (still 93%).
diagnose.principle: Legibility by scale, not zoom: the fragment is the frame, so text is readable with no camera.

diagnose.observation: Each new message gets 1.6–2.0 s before the thread scrolls.
diagnose.principle: Read time before motion: nothing moves while something is still being read.

diagnose.observation: Scrolls peak at 0.50; card exits peak at 0.70–0.92.
diagnose.principle: Arrival and departure get different curves: symmetric for moves on screen, ease-in for exits.

teaches.text: Lock the camera while the app's own content moves (typing, posting, scrolling): still 93% of the time.
teaches.setting: camera: no push while a scene's content changes in place

teaches.text: Give new content 1.6–2.0 s to be read before the next motion.
End on a claim card (1.4–2.0 s) and a logo card (4.2 s); cards leave by scaling to ×0.95 and fading, accelerating out over ~0.4 s.

critique.like: Every motion is information arriving, so the eye never has to choose between the camera and the content.
critique.wish: The logo card holds 4.2 s, 14% of the runtime, longer than any product beat.
critique.wonder: Could cutscene hold a scene's camera until new text has had its reading time, then move?
